findings.citation_support: kotlinlang.org/community and kotlinlang.org/docs/faq.html pages describe Slack, forums, meetups, and KotlinConf as active community channels.
findings.observation: Kotlin maintains an official, actively updated documentation site with a dedicated Community section listing Slack, blog, forums, and events.

findings.cell: Stack Overflow presence and survey ranking
findings.citation_support: By 2018 the Kotlin tag was already described as growing on Stack Overflow; JetBrains' own account of the 2025 Stack Overflow Developer Survey states Kotlin's usage ranking, and Stack Overflow's own 2025 blog post discusses Kotlin's community growth beyond Android.
findings.observation: Kotlin's Stack Overflow tag has grown from an already-substantial base and Kotlin is tracked as a distinct, ranked technology in the annual Stack Overflow Developer Survey.

findings.citation_support: Kotlin's own FAQ and Slack code-of-conduct pages describe a large multi-channel Slack community with formal moderators, and developer.android.com links to it as a recommended official resource.
findings.observation: Kotlin has a large, JetBrains-adjacent Slack community with dozens of active topical channels and a moderation structure, referenced directly from the official docs and from Android's official developer resources page.

findings.citation_support: kotlinconf.com describes KotlinConf as the official JetBrains-run Kotlin conference with talks, workshops and community events, with a 2027 edition already announced.
findings.observation: KotlinConf is JetBrains' official annual conference dedicated to the language, with published upcoming dates, workshops, and community programming.

findings.citation_support: Class Central lists over 800 Kotlin online courses for 2026 across providers such as Udemy, Coursera, and Udacity.
findings.observation: Independent course aggregators list several hundred Kotlin-focused online courses spanning multiple platforms and skill levels.

findings.citation_support: Class Central's 2026 best-courses guide names 'Kotlin in Action, Second Edition' as the go-to book, written by the language's lead developers and designers.
findings.observation: Kotlin has a widely-cited, authoritative book co-authored by the language's own designers, used as a standard reference in third-party learning guides.

limitations: Raw counts (Stack Overflow tag size, Slack member counts) are used only as one declared proxy among several and are not the sole basis for the score, per methodology guidance against single-proxy scoring.

The precise current Stack Overflow tag question count for Kotlin could not be freshly re-verified beyond a 2018 baseline figure (~16k, described as growing) within the fixed search budget for this task; the 2025 Developer Survey usage/admiration rankings and Stack Overflow's own 2025 blog commentary on Kotlin's community growth were used as more current corroborating signals instead.
Course-aggregator and book citations reflect third-party curation rather than a single canonical benchmark, consistent with the requirement to avoid raw popularity counts as a standalone proxy.
metric.community_public_knowledge_availa.normalization_rationale: Kotlin has a well-established, actively maintained knowledge ecosystem: official JetBrains-run documentation and community portal, a large dedicated Slack community with formal moderation, an annual official conference (KotlinConf) with continued future editions, a distinct and improving Stack Overflow Developer Survey presence, and a large third-party course/book catalog including a canonical book co-authored by the language designers. This is comparable to other mature, single-vendor-backed mainstream languages, but somewhat behind the very largest multi-decade, multi-vendor communities (e.g. JavaScript, Python, Java) in raw discussion volume, warranting a strong but not maximal score of 85/100.
metric.community_public_knowledge_availa.retrieval_route: Provider-brokered web_search tool, 4 queries executed (query terms: 'Kotlin Stack Overflow tag questions count 2026'; 'Kotlin Stack Overflow Developer Survey 2025 popularity'; 'Kotlin Slack community members KotlinConf official documentation'; 'Kotlin books O'Reilly courses Udemy Coursera 2026').
metric.community_public_knowledge_availa.selection_rule: Predeclared, language-neutral evidence cells: (1) official language documentation/community hub, (2) largest general Q&A site presence (Stack Overflow tag + language usage-share ranking from the Stack Overflow Developer Survey), (3) official/major real-time chat community, (4) official recurring conference, (5) third-party MOOC aggregator course count, (6) presence of a canonical, widely-cited book. These cells are applied identically across all assigned languages in this evaluation family.
